problem.text: Triangle $ABC$ with $AB=50$ and $AC=10$ has area $120$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, and let $E$ be the midpoint of $\overline{AC}$. The angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects $\overline{DE}$ and $\overline{BC}$ at $F$ and $G$, respectively. What is the area of quadrilateral $FDBG$?

steps.title: Where to start: a big triangle minus a small one
steps.body: The quadrilateral $FDBG$ is awkward, but its sides lie on triangle $ABG$. $D$ is on $AB$ and $F$ is on $AG$, so cutting triangle $ABG$ along $DF$ leaves $FDBG$ plus the small triangle $ADF$. So the plan is $[FDBG]=[ABG]-[ADF]$, where $[\ ]$ means area.

your_turn.prompt: What two facts about the figure will help? Think about what $G$ does to $BC$, and what $D$, $E$ do to the sides.
your_turn.answer: $AG$ is an angle bisector, so it splits $BC$ in a known ratio; and $DE$ joins two midpoints.

steps.title: Area of triangle $ABG$
steps.body: The angle bisector theorem says the bisector from $A$ cuts $BC$ in the same ratio as the two sides next to angle $A$: $\frac{BG}{GC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{50}{10}=5$. Triangles $ABG$ and $AGC$ have the same height from $A$, so their areas are in the same ratio $5:1$ as their bases.

your_turn.prompt: What fraction of the area $120$ is triangle $ABG$? Compute $[ABG]$.

steps.title: Use the midline
steps.body: The midline theorem says the segment joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side and half as long. Shrinking the whole triangle toward $A$ by a factor $\frac12$ carries $B$ to $D$ and $C$ to $E$, so it carries $BC$ onto $DE$ and $G$ onto $F$. So $F$ is the midpoint of $AG$, and triangle $ADF$ is triangle $ABG$ shrunk by $\frac12$ from $A$. Careful: lengths halve, but areas do not.

your_turn.prompt: If every length of a triangle is halved, what happens to its area?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
$[ADF]=\frac14\cdot100=25$, so
$$[FDBG]=[ABG]-[ADF]=100-25=75.$$
Check: $[ADE]=\frac{120}{4}=30$, and the bisector splits $DE$ in the ratio $DF:FE=AD:AE=25:5=5:1$, so $[ADF]=\frac56\cdot30=25$ again. The answer is **(D)**.

wrong_choices.C: $70$ comes from subtracting all of triangle $ADE$ (area $30$) from $[ABG]=100$. Only the part $ADF$ lies inside triangle $ABG$; the piece $AFE$ is on the other side of the bisector.
